newsitem.title: USA: Court dismisses firm's suit to stop CFTC probe.
newsitem.headline: Court dismisses firm's suit to stop CFTC probe.

text.p: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Monday a federal judge in Manhattan dismissed a lawsuitbbrought against it by a firm seeking to stop an investigation by the agency.
The dismissal was ordered by Judge John Koeltl against AVCO Financial Corp, a Greenwich, Conn., software developer, the CFTC said.

The CFTC opened a probe in January to determine whether there was fraud in the promotion of AVCO's trade-signalling computer program "Recurrence," which charts data on Swiss franc futures market and assists in analyzing that market.
In Apri, AVCO went to court to stop the investigation, saying the firm was not a commodity trading advisor and therefore beyond the enforcement juristiction of the CFTC.
The firm contended that any effort to investigate it and subject it to CFTC regulation infringed on its right of free commercial speech under the First Amendment.
CFTC is the federal agency that regulates the nation's futures markets.
In June, Koeltl denied AVCO's motion to preliminarily enjoin the CFTC investigation, pending a final decision on the complaint.
In his latest ruling, Koeltl granted the CFTC's motion to dismiss the AVCO lawsuit, saying the doctrine of sovereign immunity barred actions to block CFTC investigations.
Koeltl also ruled that AVCO's claims were not "ripe" for adjudication.
A lawyer representing AVCO was not immediately available to comment.
